item.title: Optimization of Urban Shortest Path Considering Traffic Congestion and Air Quality Using ICAW and Genetic Algorithm (Case Study: Tehran)
item.description: International Journal of Engineering — This study proposes a multi-objective framework for optimizing urban shortest paths by simultaneously considering traffic congestion and air quality. The objective is to minimize a weighted combination of travel time and pollutant exposure, with binary decision variables representing route selection. Real-world air quality data (SO₂, NO₂, CO) were collected from IoT sensors on 500 vehicles and 50 fixed stations across Tehran, integrated with traffic data via spatio-temporal synchronization using inverse distance weighting and 500m grid mapping. item.title: Next Generation Intelligent Transportation through Disaster Aware Privacy Preserving Federated Learning
item.description: International Journal of Engineering — The growing challenges posed by rapid urbanization and increased vehicle density have highlighted the need for precise and privacy-preserving traffic flow prediction models. Traditional centralized learning methods involve aggregating privacy-sensitive traffic flow data, which poses severe privacy, scalability, and governance issues. item.description: Computers, materials & continua/Computers, materials & continua (Print) — Fire threatens human life, property, and ecosystems, and recent years have seen frequent fire incidents worldwide. Video surveillance combined with deep learning has become a common strategy for fire and smoke detection. However, existing detectors often lose accuracy and robustness when targets are small, amorphous, or blurred against complex outdoor backgrounds. item.description: PhilPapers (PhilPapers Foundation) — Segregation research increasingly measures who people encounter beyond home, yet physical mobility, place semantics, and digital activity are often combined without clear construct boundaries. This study develops a physical--digital activity-space framework that distinguishes co-presence, digital exposure, and digital interaction, and represents physical and digital segregation as separate components rather than a forced composite. item.title: SUSTAINABLE MOBILITY AND TERRITORIAL ACCESSIBILITY IN MANIZALES, COLOMBIA: SOCIAL COST-BENEFIT ANALYSIS OF AN EXPANDED AERIAL CABLE NETWORK
item.description: GeoJournal of Tourism and Geosites — This research evaluates the socioeconomic feasibility of expanding the aerial cable car system in Manizales and Villamaría, Colombia, through a Social Cost-Benefit Analysis (SCBA). The assessment compares the three operational lines with a projected nine-line network, based on the Manizales Land Use Plan. The objective is to quantify and monetize impacts on CO2eq emissions, territorial accessibility, road safety, and public health benefits derived from induced active mobility. item.title: The Geography of Euroleague Basketball: Spatial Inequality, Travel Exposure and Home-Court Advantage in a Transnational League
item.description: Geosport for Society — This study conceptualizes the EuroLeague as a transnational urban network and tests whether spatial position and nominal travel distance are associated with competitive outcomes. The design integrates three empirical layers: (i) a longitudinal spatial panel covering the league-format era from 2016-17 to 2025-26; (ii) a completed 2025- 26 cross-section of 20 clubs in 17 nominal urban nodes and 11 countries; and (iii) a game-level model based on 1,943 available regular-season games from seven analytically retained seasons between 2016-17 and 2024-25. item.description: GeoJournal of Tourism and Geosites — Tourism in Goa is concentrated along the coastal belt, generating congestion, environmental stress, and uneven spatial development. This study develops a spatial decision-support framework to identify areas where tourism pressure should be contained and areas where diversification is more feasible. The analysis uses a 1 × 1 km grid across Goa and integrates tourism amenity indicators, environmental conditions, accessibility measures, and regulatory constraints. item.description: GeoJournal of Tourism and Geosites — Accurate delineation of agricultural field boundaries is essential for agro-production monitoring, irrigation management, and sustainable land use planning. Manual digitization is labour-intensive and poorly scalable, while conventional segmentation algorithms are sensitive to spectral heterogeneity and weak inter-field contrast. The Zhetysai district of southern Kazakhstan – where approximately 45-50% of irrigated farmland exhibits salinization – exemplifies the urgent demand for automated field mapping. item.title: MORE MONUMENTS, MORE TOURISTS? EXAMINING HERITAGE-TOURISM RELATIONSHIPS ACROSS ROMANIAN COUNTIES
item.description: GeoJournal of Tourism and Geosites — Cultural heritage is an important territorial resource for tourism development, yet the relationship between the distribution of listed heritage assets and tourism activity remains insufficiently understood. This study examines the geographical relationships between listed cultural heritage and tourism in Romania, focusing on territorial disparities and long-term changes. item.title: Rethinking Women’s Football Attendance in an Emerging Destination: Constraints, Marketing Awareness and Interest through a Pluriversal Lens
item.description: Geosport for Society — Women’s football is increasingly recognised as an important component of the sport tourism industry, with potential to diversify audiences, stimulate domestic travel, and advance gender inclusivity in emerging destinations. Yet, despite the growing interest, attendance remains inconsistent, complicating conventional measures of spectator demand. item.description: Revista de Aplicaciones de la Ingeniería — In this article we highlight the importance of monitoring polluting particles in cities. item.description: Journal of Maritime Policy Science. — Illegal trade in lobster pueruli (Benih Bening Lobster, BBL) presents interconnected challenges for fisheries governance, coastal livelihoods, and Indonesia’s maritime defense. This study examines how changes in BBL utilization policies, legal market access, and commodity traceability create potential vulnerabilities that may be exploited by smuggling networks. item.description: Journal of Maritime Policy Science. — Indonesia’s customs administration operates at the intersection of maritime mobility, trade facilitation, border protection, and revenue assurance, yet its risk systems are still primarily organized around declarations, manifests, entities, and transactions rather than the wider maritime operating picture. This article develops a conceptual model for transforming Maritime Domain Awareness into a Customs Risk Picture that can support earlier, more contextual, and more explainable targeting of vessels, voyages, cargoes, and commercial actors. item.title: Between emergency and reconstruction: Territorial impacts and climate adaptation challenges after hurricane John in Guerrero
item.description: ECORFAN eBooks — This chapter analyses the territorial, human, and socioeconomic impacts caused by Hurricane John (2024) in the state of Guerrero, with a particular focus on the municipalities of Acapulco and Coyuca de Benítez, within a context of increasing intensity and frequency of extreme hydrometeorological events. item.description: Jurnal Al-Ijtimaiyyah — The 2021 eruption of Mount Semeru not only destroyed homes but also severed the social and economic networks of thousands of families in Lumajang Regency, demanding a disaster response grounded in Islamic normative principles alongside technical capacity. item.description: AIS Electronic Library (AISeL) — Digital content platforms must recommend new content before knowing its quality or audience fit, while early feedback is selectively shaped by prior allocation rules. Although exploration may support learning, direct evidence is limited regarding whether early random exploration improves the subsequent organic recommendation performance of new content by generating more informative feedback. item.title: Contribution of agricultural cooperatives and humanitarian assistance on food security resilience and rural development in Mali
item.description: ORBi (University of Liège) — Mali, located in the Sahel region, experiences a persistent food security crisis driven by climate variability, recurrent conflict, displacement, market disruptions, and structural weaknesses in rural systems. The agricultural sector, which supports the majority of households, is highly vulnerable to droughts, erratic rainfall, flooding, and insecurity. item.title: Comparative Framework of Vulnerability in Coastal Communities of the Ecuadorian Tropics
item.description: Applied Planetary Health — This study conducts a comparative analysis of socio-ecological vulnerability in six coastal communities of the Ecuadorian tropics, integrating mixed methods (quantitative and qualitative). The conceptual framework based on the components of Exposure, Sensitivity, and Adaptive Capacity allowed the construction of a Comparative Coastal Vulnerability Index (CCVI). item.title: Eco-feminism in the modern world: Gender, environment and social transformation
item.description: International Journal of Research in English — Eco-feminism is an interdisciplinary intellectual and social movement that connects gender equality, environmental sustainability and social justice. It examines how systems of patriarchy, economic exploitation, unequal resource distribution and environmental degradation can reinforce one another. item.description: Digital Commons - USU (Utah State University) — This research explored how access to everyday destinations influences neighborhood and social satisfaction among individuals with disabilities. It examined how factors such as sociodemographic characteristics, accessibility, and frequency of visits to places contribute to how people experience their neighborhoods and social lives. item.description: PubMed Central — Background: Climate change is increasing the extent of wildfires and extreme heat events (EHEs) in the Western United States. item.description: AHFE international — The presented study investigates associations between events influencing public transportation experience in both urban (Hamburg) and rural (Tuttlingen) areas in Germany, with the aim of identifying events associated with travel experience, which may in turn influence travel behavior. Using a mobile application, 21 participants in Tuttlingen and 70 participants in Hamburg tracked everyday trips, providing real-time evaluations of travel experiences along with situational data. item.title: Stormwater Runoff from the University of Southern California, University Park Campus: Potential Hazards and Drivers of Dissolved and Particulate Pollution
item.description: EarthArXiv (California Digital Library) — Climate models predict that Southern California will begin experiencing longer periods of drought and more intense storms in the coming decades. Long periods of drought have the potential to allow for the buildup of pollutants on undisturbed areas, such as the roofs of buildings and in gutters. item.description: Research Square — Walking-supportive neighborhoods are important for population health, yet macroscale walkability indices can obscure street-level conditions and their equitable distribution. This cross-sectional study explored how neighborhood income and demographic composition relate to microscale pedestrian infrastructure and whether these income-related differences in microscale features are moderated by macroscale walkability. item.description: Research Square — (150 words) Urban overheating threatens efforts to expand low-carbon active mobility, yet cities lack scalable methods to identify where heat most affects cyclists. This study integrates high-resolution biometeorological modeling with segment-based cycling mobility data to distinguish between heat hazard and actual heat exposure. item.title: Assessment of the Socioeconomic Impacts of Floods in Bugarama Valley, Rusizi District, Rwanda
item.description: East African Journal of Environment and Natural Resources — Flooding is a major natural hazard that continues to affect livelihoods and socioeconomic development in Bugarama Valley, Rusizi District, Rwanda. Due to its low-lying topography and proximity to the Rusizi River and wetlands, the valley frequently experiences flooding caused by intense rainfall, river overflow, and poor drainage systems. item.description: Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence — Extreme weather events expose the semantic limitations of numerical traffic forecasting models across urban transportation networks. item.description: Proceedings of the Prehistoric Society — This paper applies resilience theory as a heuristic framework to examine regional differences in the Anatolian peninsula during the millennium after 5500 BC when we find a general contraction in permanent open-air settlements. item.description: Ecological civilization — The world’s largest contiguous mangrove forest and among the most climate-vulnerable social-ecological systems, the transboundary Sundarbans is shared by Bangladesh and India. item.description: Discover Environment — Early warning systems reduce disaster risk only when forecast information is converted into timely, trusted and feasible action. This article examines why that conversion remains difficult in Mogadishu, Somalia, a fragile and rapidly urbanising city exposed to flooding, displacement and weak urban services. item.title: Methodological framework for tsunami risk assessment in port facilities
item.description: Natural hazards and earth system sciences — Although tsunami hazard modeling has advanced significantly, the development of asset-specific vulnerability functions and risk indicators at the terminal scale remains a critical challenge, hindering the effective integration of scientific knowledge into port infrastructure planning and risk management. item.description: Frontiers in Education — Introduction Armed conflicts pose significant challenges to maintaining inclusive education (IE) by disrupting educational continuity, displacing students and teachers, and increasing the diversity and complexity of learners’ needs. item.description: Frontiers in Science — Global fertility rates have declined rapidly and universally in recent decades and most nations now have rates below replacement level. item.description: Preprint / source unavailable — Despite sustained public investment and existing regulatory frameworks, the peri-urban Mefou watershed in Yaoundé’s 7th arrondissement, Cameroon, remains vulnerable to recurrent flooding. item.title: Anatomy of mapping urban greenery from a human perspective
item.description: Environmental Data Science — Urban greenery contributes to environmental sustainability, livability, and human well-being. As interest in human-centered urban environments has grown, researchers have increasingly sought to measure greenery as it is experienced by people rather than solely through conventional top-down representations. Advances in street-level imagery, computer vision, machine learning, and geospatial analysis have enabled this shift, resulting in a rapidly expanding but methodologically diverse body of literature. item.title: The Economic Dynamics of City Structure: Evidence from Hiroshima’s Recovery
item.description: Journal of Political Economy — We provide new theory and evidence on the resilience of internal city structure after a large shock, analyzing the atomic bombing of Hiroshima. Exploiting newly digitized data, we document that the city structure recovered within five years after the bombing. Our new dynamic quantitative model of internal city structure incorporates commuting, forward-looking location choices, migration frictions, agglomeration forces, and heterogeneous location fundamentals. item.title: Salutogenic urban housing in hot-arid climates: Daylight as a catalyst for health and resilience
item.description: E3S Web of Conferences — This paper provides a critical, integrated examination on the built environment of hot-arid Levantine cities, specifically evaluating its unintended, long-term impacts on human health. Gropius championed a functionalist architecture of standardization, extensive glazing, and flat roofs designed to maximize “sun, light, and air”. item.title: Nuclear invisibilities
item.description: Routledge eBooks — Koodankulam, on India’s southern coast, has witnessed one of the country’s longest-running women-led antinuclear movements, which intensified in the wake of the 2011 Fukushima nuclear accident. Shared community spaces, conventionally sites of communal childcare and traditional livelihood practices, transformed into sites of exceptional protest when the communities were confronted with the imposition of a nuclear power plant. item.title: The Demographic Impact of Leadership: Mayoral Education and COVID‐19 Excess Mortality in Italy
item.description: Population and Development Review — During the COVID‐19 pandemic, excess mortality rose sharply across Europe, with striking territorial disparities even within countries. This paper examines whether the characteristics of locally elected officials influenced excess mortality in Italy—one of the first countries severely affected. Using weekly death statistics and a Bayesian hierarchical spatiotemporal model, we estimate excess mortality at the municipal level. item.title: Differences in extreme weather risk communication channels: how channel-specific information exposure shapes older adults’ psychological resilience
item.description: Frontiers in Psychology — Introduction This study focuses on older adults, a large and vulnerable population within China’s social structure, and draws upon risk perception theory and psychological resilience theory to examine the association between risk information exposure and psychological resilience among older adults. Methods The quantitative analysis was based on 634 valid questionnaires collected from older adults aged 60 years and older. item.title: Green Infrastructure Development and Implications for Urban Sustainability, Public Health, and Climate Resilience, Al Khoud, Oman
item.description: E3S Web of Conferences — Rapid urban development in Oman, particularly in Al Khoud, Muscat, has placed increasing pressure on the environment, leading to a growing shortage of green space. This has raised concerns about urban heat, outdoor comfort, and the overall livability of urban areas. This study examines the current state of green infrastructure (GI) in Al Khoud and its contribution to a comfortable urban living environment. item.title: Landscapes and Extractive Livelihood Lock-In: A Spatial Macro Psychological Analysis of Slow-Onset Environmental Degradation, Collective Efficacy, and Communal Disorganization in the Bangka Belitung Archipelago, Indonesia
item.description: Jurnal Multidisiplin Indonesia — Slow-onset environmental degradation associated with open-pit tin mining and coastal ecosystem deterioration has transformed ecological conditions and livelihoods in extractive island regions. However, environmental psychology research has predominantly emphasized individual cognitive responses and acute disasters, providing limited understanding of how ecological degradation and extractive economic dependence interact to shape community-level psychosocial vulnerability. item.title: Geospatial Assessment of Rainfall-Triggered Landslide Risk Using Multi-Criteria Decision Techniques in Venezuela
item.description: Progress in landslide research and technology — Rainfall-induced landslides are a persistent threat in Venezuela due to a combination of varied topography, tropical rainfall and rapid urbanisation on alluvial fans and unstable hillslopes. This chapter aims to produce national Landslide Risk Index Maps (LRiM) to support disaster reduction initiatives in the country. Multi-Criteria Decision Methods (MCDM), geographic information systems and remote-sensing techniques were used to generate the LRiM, considering hazard, exposure, and vulnerability indicators. item.title: Urban heat islands, climate change, and evolving disease landscapes in India: A public health review
item.description: Journal of Preventive Medicine and Holistic Health — The convergence of the Urban Heat Island (UHI) phenomenon, accelerating climate change, and unchecked urban expansion has produced a public health emergency of unprecedented scale across India. Localized microclimatic warming is reshaping the epidemiology of both infectious and chronic disease, altering the transmission dynamics of vector-borne, re-emerging, and neglected tropical illnesses. item.title: Vulnerability of traditional villages in ethnic minority areas: terrain gradient and cultural accessibility effects — evidence from 1325 villages in Sichuan, China
item.description: Preprint / source unavailable — Traditional villages are the spatial carriers of living ethnic minority culture, and their persistence directly affects the quality of rural revitalization in ethnic minority areas. Existing vulnerability studies mostly take natural hazards or tourism disturbance as the source of stress, and rarely consider whether villages can obtain cultural resources nearby. This study takes 1325 traditional villages at or above the provincial level in the 21 cities (prefectures) of Sichuan Province as its sample, of which 506 are in the three prefectures of Ganzi, Aba and Liangshan, accounting for 38.2%. item.title: Remediation and immobilization of hexavalent chromium in contaminated soil using Cordia africana leaf-derived biochar
item.description: Discover Environment — Soil pollution from hexavalent chromium (Cr(VI)) poses severe risks to ecosystems and food security due to its high mobility and toxicity. This study evaluated the capacity of Cordia africana leaf-derived biochar to remediate and immobilize Cr(VI) in contaminated silty clay soil. The biochar, produced via controlled pyrolysis, exhibited a highly porous structure with a specific surface area of 698.813 m²/g and surface functional groups including hydroxyl, carboxyl, and aromatic rings. item.title: Modeling superblocks in central Thessaloniki: A PTV Visum-based traffic assessment
item.description: E3S Web of Conferences — Superblocks restrict through-traffic within groups of urban blocks and reallocate street space to walking, cycling, greenery, and public life. This paper assesses the traffic implications of applying the model in central Thessaloniki. We developed a macroscopic PTV Visum model for the central area bounded by Egnatia Street, Nikis Avenue, Dodekanisou-Salaminos Streets, and N. Germanou-Angelaki Streets. item.title: Standardization landscape for positive energy districts: mapping SDOs, gaps, and recommendations for interoperability
item.description: Frontiers in Energy Research — Positive Energy Districts (PEDs) have emerged as a transformative paradigm for urban decarbonization, yet their implementation requires integration across energy systems, buildings, mobility, and information and communication technologies, for which no coherent international standardization framework currently exists. This conceptual analysis examines the PED standardization landscape using a three-layer interoperability model encompassing technical, governance, and social dimensions. item.description: Scientific Reports — Air pollution may be associated with cognitive ageing, with variation in exposure–response shape and effect modification. item.title: Optical GeoAI and spatial modeling enable urban-canopy mapping and resilience screening in Davis, California
item.description: Frontiers in Sustainability — Cities need spatially explicit canopy information to connect urban greening with surface-temperature context, mobility, and neighborhood planning. We developed an optical GeoAI workflow for Davis, California, using 2022 National Agriculture Imagery Program (0.6 m RGB + NIR). item.title: Flexible but not free: The gendered flexibility paradox in Indonesia's gig economy
item.description: SIMULACRA JURNAL SOSIOLOGI — Female gig workers in Indonesia face challenges underexamined in a gig economy literature centered largely on Western contexts. Domestic scholarship has tended to treat gender as a descriptive variable within male-dominated sectors. This study examines how platform algorithms, gender norms, and household responsibilities shape women’s gig work across sectors. item.title: From ashes to agency: informal-settlement fires, intergenerational power, and democratic survival in Gauteng, South Africa
item.description: Frontiers in Sociology — Introduction Recurrent fires in South Africa's informal settlements are governed as technical emergencies, despite being produced and experienced through unequal infrastructures, insecure tenure, and uneven state protection. This study examines how young and older residents of fire-prone informal settlements in the Ekurhuleni Metropolitan Municipality interpret risk, respond to emergencies, negotiate recovery, and convert disaster experience into civic action.
